name: IM-3D
text:
# IM-3D
## Overview
IM-3D is a 3D reconstruction method that fine-tunes an image-to-video model based on Emu to generate a turn-table style video rotating around an object, which is subsequently used as input for [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) reconstruction [S1][S2, unofficial]. It builds on [Orbit Camera Path Generation](7811-orbit-camera-path-generation.md) by generating the orbiting frames via a learned video model rather than explicit camera [trajectory sampling](#6410-camera-trajectory-and-path-generation.md).
## How it works
**Inputs and Outputs:**
*   **Input:** A single source image of the target object [G].
*   **Output:** A [3D Gaussian Splatting representation](#2257-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs-preliminaries.md) of the object [S1][S2, unofficial].
**Data Structures:**
*   **Fine-tuned Image-to-Video Model:** An Emu-based architecture adapted for turn-table video generation [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **Generated Video:** A sequence of frames simulating a camera orbiting the object [S1][S2, unofficial].
*   **[3DGS Representation](#12855-gaussian-representation-and-truncation.md):** The final output structure containing Gaussian attributes (position, covariance, color, opacity) derived from the video frames [S1][S2, unofficial].
**Steps:**
1.  **[Fine-tuning](#9138-fine-tuning.md):** The Emu-based image-to-video model is fine-tuned [S1][S2, unofficial].
2.  **Video Generation:** The fine-tuned model takes the single input image and generates a video sequence where the camera rotates around the object [S1][S2, unofficial].
3.  **3DGS Reconstruction:** The generated video frames are extracted and fed into a 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) reconstruction pipeline to recover the 3D scene [S1][S2, unofficial].
**Parameters:**
*   **[Rotation](#19376-rotation.md) Angle:** Not given in the sources. [S1][S2, unofficial]
*   **Video Length:** Not given in the sources. [S1][S2, unofficial]

## Background
IM-3D was introduced in the context of recent advances in 3D Gaussian Splatting [S1][S2, unofficial]. It builds upon the Emu image-to-video model [S1][S2, unofficial] and applies it to the task of single-image 3D reconstruction via intermediate video generation.
